## Interpretation

**Headline — realism weakens the implant, not the leakage.** Swapping canned one-line agreements for the model's own judge-filtered agreeing completions — holding prompts, personas, row counts, ratios, and the full #411 recipe fixed — cuts the installed sycophancy dose from ~0.90 to ~0.63 self-implant Δ. Putting the same completions behind a 3-turn on-policy conversational prefix (identical loss-bearing tokens; the prefix is the only change) cuts it again to ~0.50, and villain's prefix cells never clear the +0.50 install floor. Both gaps are sign-consistent in every covered cell and seed and are flat-from-epoch-1 asymptotes. Meanwhile mean bystander leakage stays within ~0.02 of the canned arm. Two readings travel together: (i) low-entropy canned templates are simply easier to fit at fixed steps — realistic data buys less behavior per gradient step; (ii) per unit of installed behavior, the realistic arms leak MORE (0.15 → 0.18 → 0.24), directionally OPPOSITE to the plan's weak prior that the conversational prefix would anchor the behavior to the trained persona. Neither registered leakage contrast survives as a registered call (dose confound + 2-source coverage), but the install-strength gradient is the cleanest result in the run.

**The yield walls are a finding, not just missingness.** For half the sources the realistic rig cannot be built at all: under the kindergarten_teacher and software_engineer personas the base model refuses to agree with false claims often enough that 36 rounds x 8 samples of agreement-opener prefill left 6 and 31 of 200 rows unfilled. On-policy sycophancy data does not exist for personas whose role priors resist agreement — the canned rig was teaching those personas text they would never produce. This makes the data-realism critique of the old rig concrete, and it constrains every future on-policy sycophancy design: source selection is gated by elicitability.

**The anomaly survives where testable, and the dense panel sharpens it.** The assistant-twins stay flat (mildly negative, CIs excluding 0) under the canned software_engineer adapter, replicating #591. The designed realistic-arm test never ran (G3 drop). But the software_engineer curve reframes the anomaly: on a panel dense in assistant-like and teacher near-twins, this adapter's leakage is broad and cosine-INVERTED (rho −0.47) — role/prior appears to gate leakage more than geometry for this source, though prior-cosine collinearity (−0.65) blocks a clean separation. The same collinearity fired for 3 of 4 sources, which is itself an instrument lesson: base sycophancy prior and persona-space proximity could not be decorrelated below |Pearson| 0.6 with the realizable persona pool — they are entangled properties of role semantics.

**What this run does NOT establish.** (1) Whether on-policy data changes the leakage-vs-cosine RADIUS (the Goal's first question) is indeterminate: the endpoint contrast is dose-confounded (spread 0.40) and covers 2 sources; the pre-registered dose-matched read (band-entry checkpoints) requires new full-panel evals on the uploaded epoch-1/2 checkpoints. (2) The prefix arm's weaker install is measured by SINGLE-TURN probes; the trained behavior may be partly conditioned on conversational context the eval never supplies — "weaker install" vs "context-gated install" is undecided. (3) The on-policy bundle moves provenance + length + diversity together (named in plan §12); the component driving the weaker install is not decomposed. (4) Tier-2 elicit-and-strip dominates the on-policy pools (62–83% of positives), so "on-policy" here mostly means "model-written under an agree instruction, trained without it" — the published persona-vectors dataset shape, not bare on-policy sampling.

## Interpretation

**Headline — the on-policy data bundle installs the behavior far more weakly; what happens to leakage is unresolved.** Swapping canned one-line agreements for the model's own judge-filtered agreeing completions — holding prompts, personas, row counts, ratios, and the full #411 recipe fixed — cuts the installed sycophancy dose from ~0.90 to ~0.63 self-implant Δ. Per plan §12 this swap moves provenance, length, diversity, and elicitation tier TOGETHER: the result is "the on-policy/elicited-response bundle installs more weakly at the fixed recipe", not a decomposed effect of realism per se. Putting the same completions behind a 3-turn conversational prefix (identical loss-bearing tokens; the prefix is the only change) reads another ~0.13 lower on single-turn probes — but that lower reading is ambiguous between weaker installation and context-gated installation the single-turn eval cannot see. Both gaps are sign-consistent in every covered cell and seed and are flat-from-epoch-1 asymptotes (per-cell SE ≈ 0.02 against arm-mean gaps of 0.27 and 0.13). Bystander leakage at the endpoint stays within ~0.02 of the canned arm at the point estimate, but the registered contrast is INDETERMINATE (CI [−0.055, +0.015] — compatible with anything from a ~40% relative reduction to a small increase), K2-demoted, and dose-confounded; the leakage-radius question is unresolved pending the dose-matched band-entry read. The exploratory leakage-per-dose ratio (0.15 → 0.18 → 0.24) is reported descriptively only — a concave dose-response produces the same pattern mechanically.

**Content agreement weakens; the sycophantic style installs broadly.** The judge-verified self rates measure content-level agreement with the false claim. Underneath them, roughly half of the on-policy arms' NON-agreeing responses (52% single-turn, 38% prefix, vs 2–7% base) open with an explicit agreement phrase before correcting. The on-policy arms are not failing to learn sycophancy — they are learning a broader, shallower form of it (agreeable affect) while the canned arm's narrow form (assert the false claim) installs at near-ceiling. Any safety read of "weaker install" should carry this: the measured construct dropped; an unmeasured adjacent construct did not.

**The yield walls are a recipe-bound finding.** Under this exact fill policy (tiered elicitation, agreement-opener prefill, judge acceptance, 36 rounds x 8 samples retry budget), two of four source personas did not reach the pre-registered 200-row yield gate: kindergarten_teacher fell 6 rows short (194/200 — 97%, a near-miss against a strict per-row gate), software_engineer 31 rows short (169/200, with bare tier-1 agreement obtainable for only 11/200 rows — the genuine wall). The accurate generalization is narrower than v1 stated: under this recipe and retry budget, on-policy sycophancy data could not be completed for personas whose role priors resist agreement — not that such data "cannot be generated at all". It still makes the data-realism critique of the canned rig concrete (the canned rig taught those personas text they rarely produce), and it gates future on-policy source selection on elicitability — under this elicitation design.

**The anomaly survives where testable — with two live readings.** The assistant-twins (virtual_assistant, digital_helper; cosine 0.979 to software_engineer) stay flat-to-mildly-negative under the canned software_engineer adapter (both pooled CIs exclude 0 on the negative side), replicating #591. The designed realistic-arm test never ran (G3 drop). Two mechanisms fit these cells: (i) **role/prior gating** — the dense panel shows leakage tracking role semantics over geometry for this source (rho −0.47 inverted; school_principal +0.43 at the same cosine where the twins sit at −0.03); (ii) **suppression generalization from the trained contrastive negative** — the default `assistant` persona IS a trained negative for software_engineer in this design (neg_member_for in panel_set.json; cosine 0.969 to the source), and the probe twins are its 0.979-cosine near-twins, so mildly NEGATIVE deltas with CIs excluding 0 are exactly what trained-down corrections generalizing from `assistant` would produce. Reading (ii) changes what the anomaly means — an artifact of the training design rather than a property of the persona — and the planning round explicitly carried this fork forward. The two readings are not exclusive and this run cannot separate them: that requires an adapter whose negative set omits `assistant` (or a twin probe far from any trained negative).

**What this run does NOT establish.** (1) Whether on-policy data changes the leakage-vs-cosine RADIUS (the Goal's first question) is indeterminate: the endpoint contrast is K2-demoted, dose-confounded (spread 0.40), and covers 2 sources; the pre-registered dose-matched read (band-entry checkpoints) requires new full-panel evals on the uploaded epoch-1/2 checkpoints. (2) The prefix arm's weaker install is measured by SINGLE-TURN probes; "weaker install" vs "context-gated install" is undecided. (3) The on-policy bundle moves provenance + length + diversity + elicitation tier together (plan §12); the component driving the weaker install is not decomposed. (4) Tier-2 elicit-and-strip dominates the on-policy pools (62–83% of positives), so "on-policy" here mostly means "model-written under an agree instruction, trained without it" — the published persona-vectors dataset shape, not bare on-policy sampling. (5) The yield walls are bound to this elicitation recipe and retry budget; a different fill policy could move them.

## Interpretation

**Headline — the on-policy data bundle installs the behavior far more weakly; what happens to leakage is unresolved.** Swapping canned one-line agreements for the model's own judge-filtered agreeing completions — holding prompts, personas, row counts, ratios, and the full #411 recipe fixed — cuts the installed sycophancy dose from ~0.90 to ~0.63 self-implant Δ. Per plan §12 this swap moves provenance, length, diversity, and elicitation tier TOGETHER: the result is "the on-policy/elicited-response bundle installs more weakly at the fixed recipe", not a decomposed effect of realism per se. Putting the same completions behind a 3-turn conversational prefix (identical loss-bearing tokens; the prefix is the only change) reads another ~0.13 lower on single-turn probes — but that lower reading is ambiguous between weaker installation and context-gated installation the single-turn eval cannot see. Both gaps are sign-consistent in every covered cell and seed and are flat-from-epoch-1 asymptotes (per-cell SE ≈ 0.02 against like-for-like villain+comedian arm-mean gaps of 0.25 and 0.13). Bystander leakage at the endpoint stays within ~0.02 of the canned arm at the point estimate, but the registered contrast is INDETERMINATE (CI [−0.055, +0.015] — compatible with anything from a ~40% relative reduction to a small increase), K2-demoted, and dose-confounded; the leakage-radius question is unresolved pending the dose-matched band-entry read. The exploratory leakage-per-dose ratio (0.15 → 0.18 → 0.24) is reported descriptively only — a concave dose-response produces the same pattern mechanically.

**Content agreement weakens; the sycophantic style installs broadly.** The judge-verified self rates measure content-level agreement with the false claim. Underneath them, roughly half of the on-policy arms' NON-agreeing responses (52% single-turn, 38% prefix, vs 2–7% base) open with an explicit agreement phrase before correcting. The on-policy arms are not failing to learn sycophancy — they are learning a broader, shallower form of it (agreeable affect) while the canned arm's narrow form (assert the false claim) installs at near-ceiling. Any safety read of "weaker install" should carry this: the measured construct dropped; an unmeasured adjacent construct did not.

**The yield walls are a recipe-bound finding.** Under this exact fill policy (tiered elicitation, agreement-opener prefill, judge acceptance, 36 rounds x 8 samples retry budget), two of four source personas did not reach the pre-registered 200-row yield gate: kindergarten_teacher fell 6 rows short (194/200 — 97%, a near-miss against a strict per-row gate), software_engineer 31 rows short (169/200, with bare tier-1 agreement obtainable for only 11/200 rows — the genuine wall). The accurate generalization is narrower than v1 stated: under this recipe and retry budget, on-policy sycophancy data could not be completed for personas whose role priors resist agreement — not that such data "cannot be generated at all". It still makes the data-realism critique of the canned rig concrete (the canned rig taught those personas text they rarely produce), and it gates future on-policy source selection on elicitability — under this elicitation design.

**The anomaly survives where testable — with two live readings.** The assistant-twins (virtual_assistant, digital_helper; cosine 0.979 to software_engineer) stay flat-to-mildly-negative under the canned software_engineer adapter (both pooled CIs exclude 0 on the negative side), replicating #591. The designed realistic-arm test never ran (G3 drop). Two mechanisms fit these cells: (i) **role/prior gating** — the dense panel shows leakage tracking role semantics over geometry for this source (rho −0.47 inverted; school_principal +0.43 at the same cosine where the twins sit at −0.03); (ii) **suppression generalization from the trained contrastive negative** — the default `assistant` persona IS a trained negative for software_engineer in this design (neg_member_for in panel_set.json; cosine 0.969 to the source), and the probe twins are its 0.979-cosine near-twins, so mildly NEGATIVE deltas with CIs excluding 0 are exactly what trained-down corrections generalizing from `assistant` would produce. Reading (ii) changes what the anomaly means — an artifact of the training design rather than a property of the persona — and the planning round explicitly carried this fork forward. The two readings are not exclusive and this run cannot separate them: that requires an adapter whose negative set omits `assistant` (or a twin probe far from any trained negative).

**What this run does NOT establish.** (1) Whether on-policy data changes the leakage-vs-cosine RADIUS (the Goal's first question) is indeterminate: the endpoint contrast is K2-demoted, dose-confounded (spread 0.40), and covers 2 sources; the pre-registered dose-matched read (band-entry checkpoints) requires new full-panel evals on the uploaded epoch-1/2 checkpoints. (2) The prefix arm's weaker install is measured by SINGLE-TURN probes; "weaker install" vs "context-gated install" is undecided. (3) The on-policy bundle moves provenance + length + diversity + elicitation tier together (plan §12); the component driving the weaker install is not decomposed. (4) Tier-2 elicit-and-strip dominates the on-policy pools (62–83% of positives), so "on-policy" here mostly means "model-written under an agree instruction, trained without it" — the published persona-vectors dataset shape, not bare on-policy sampling. (5) The yield walls are bound to this elicitation recipe and retry budget; a different fill policy could move them.
